conviction_note: The Q3 quarter was effectively pre-released on 2026-09-03 ('at or above the top end' of every guided line), so the print turns on the Q4 guide. On that I have one decelerating counterparty (Progressive's September personal-lines NPW was +1%, against +5% year to date) and one mildly positive peer signal (EverQuote's $50m buyback), set against a 22.6% 20-day run-up. The findings sum to -1.2 and the scaled number is +0.22 (p_up 51 x abs 11). The gap is real: the findings lean on run-up and proxy negatives, while p_up stays near 50 because the company-level document (the pre-announcement) is positive and this name's reaction history is a coin flip (4 of 7 up). The search was cut short by an exhausted shared search budget.
bar: Company Q3 guide: revenue $330-355m, contribution $51.5-54.5m, adj. EBITDA $32-35m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000198/maxq22026-earningsreleasex.htm, 2026-07-29). The company then said on 2026-09-03 that all three would land 'at or above the top end' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818383/000181838326000229/max-20260902.htm). Street revenue consensus disagrees by source: $347.7m and EPS $0.27 per Earnings Whispers (https://finviz.com/news/405230/mediaalphas-q3-test-can-carrier-broadening-and-margin-recovery-offset-slowing-growth, 2026-10-20), against $353.8m and EPS $0.36 per Benzinga (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/MAX/earnings-forecasts). The effective bar is the pre-announced floor of $355m revenue / $54.5m contribution / $35m adj. EBITDA plus a Q4 guide nobody has sourced. Because the estimate sources disagree, every reported-quarter finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest was 3,219,791 shares, 6.16% of float, 2.8 days to cover, at the 2026-10-15 record date (published 2026-10-26). That is up 13.7% from 2,831,462 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MAX/short-interest/), so not a crowded short. Baseline skew is -10.16 vol points (upside paid) and put/call OI is 0.41, but the ATM spread is 96% of mid, so the chain is not a usable statement. Run-up is +22.57% over 20 days, +1.82% over 5 days, and the stock is 17.8% below its 52-week high. The founder/CEO is a steady 10b5-1 seller: a 13D/A dated 2026-08-26 shows a net 725k-share decrease and 9.8% ownership.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-03 MediaAlpha raised its Q3 outlook to 'at or above the top end' on all three guided lines: revenue at least $355m (+~16% YoY, against a guide midpoint of $342.5m / +12%), contribution at least $54.5m and adj. EBITDA at least $35m. The Earnings Whispers consensus dated 2026-10-20 still sits at $347.7m revenue, below that floor; Benzinga's sits at $353.8m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue came in at $316.9m, above the top of a $290-310m guide, with every line of the outlook raised, and the stock moved -1.88% (2026-07-29). This name does not reliably pay for a revenue beat; its last 7 reactions were 4 up and 3 down at a median absolute 14%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: it is a public Reg FD 8-K, and the stock still fell to about $9.40 by 2026-09-25 before the run-up. The only unpriced part is the 'or above' tail and estimate sources that lag it ($347.7m). If it were fully priced, every consensus would sit at or above $355m.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-20 says management beat its own revenue range for two straight quarters (https://finviz.com/news/405230/mediaalphas-q3-test-can-carrier-broadening-and-margin-recovery-offset-slowing-growth). That is the same company pattern, not an independent datum.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09 MediaAlpha bought out PLX's share of the Tax Receivable Agreement for $12.0m cash, against $22.7m of TRA liability attributable to PLX, a $10.7m (47%) discount. This should produce a Q3 non-operating gain of roughly $10m (Q2's $37.7m TRA gain was booked in other income) and cuts the remaining TRA liability to about $32m. GAAP EPS is likely to land mechanically above the $0.27 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's $37.7m TRA gain pushed EPS to $0.65 against $0.23, and the stock moved -1.88%. The market looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: A headline-EPS 'beat' generated by the gain may print in wire copy. The gain sits below operating income and has no path to the guide, so it is worth a fraction of the same dollars as operating profit. The part with real value is the ~$10m less of future cash TRA payments, which modestly helps FCF.
findings.independence: The Q2 release documents that the prior TRA repurchase was booked as a $37.7m gain in other income (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000198/maxq22026-earningsreleasex.htm). Same company, different filing.

findings.finding: Progressive is the dominant P&C advertiser; MAX's three >10% customers were 57% of Q2 revenue, and P&C is 97% of revenue. Its 2026-10-14 Q3 release shows September Personal Lines NPW +1% YoY against +5% year to date, a sharp deceleration. Policies in force still grew (agency auto +7%, direct auto +8%), the Q3 combined ratio was 88.7 against 89.5, and the release carries no advertising commentary. This bears on the Q4 guide, which depends on carrier budgets in Oct-Dec. Net of the rest: the 3rd-5th largest carriers nearly quadrupled spend in H1 2026, which partly offsets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large moves on this name have historically tracked the carrier-spend outlook in the guide: -18.49% in Feb 2025, -14.9% in Apr 2026, +15.44% in Feb 2026. I cannot source which line drove each.
findings.why_not_priced: Weakly priced at most. MAX rose 9.3% on 2026-10-15, the day after this release, and has run up 22.6% in 20 days, which is not what a market reading the NPW deceleration as a demand cut looks like. If priced, MAX would have sold off after 10-14. Caveat: NPW can slow on rate cuts rather than on volume, and PIF growth of 7-8% with an 88.7 CR leaves room to advertise. That is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: The proxy is not confirmed by MAX. Progressive's own Q2 10-Q said it will keep advertising while on track for its profitability goal (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000308/pgr-20260630.htm), which cuts the other way. The concentration figures are from the MAX Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818383/000181838326000200/max-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Growth decelerates mechanically into H2. The Q3 guide implied +12% YoY at the midpoint against +26% in Q2, management warned of tougher back-half comparisons, and Q2 contribution grew only 18% on 26% revenue growth because take rates dipped. A Q4 guide implying single-digit or low-teens growth is the likely shape of the forward line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-04-29 the stock fell 14.9% on a print whose guide/line driver I could not source. On 2026-07-29 a beat with a raised guide moved -1.88%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is in the wire preview. Filed because the run-up of 22.6% raises the bar the Q4 guide must clear. If priced, the stock would not have re-rated toward its 50-day average ($11.46) into the print.
findings.independence: The Q2 release's Q3 guide shows the +12% midpoint (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000198/maxq22026-earningsreleasex.htm). It is the same company data seen through the preview, so not fully independent.

findings.finding: Peer EverQuote (auto-insurance lead-gen, same carrier customers) announced a $50m buyback on 2026-10-21, ahead of its own Q3 print. Its CFO cited 'strong free cash flow' and 'confidence in the company's ongoing growth trajectory', and it amended its credit agreement to permit up to $75m of repurchases. There was no preliminary Q3 number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced history of MAX reacting to EverQuote corporate actions.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer buyback is not a demand number, and the market may have read it already: the MAX run-up continued after 10-21. It is a weak positive read on the carrier-spend environment into October, i.e. into Q4.
findings.independence: 8-K body for the same event: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1640428/000119312526427815/ever-20261021.htm (same document set).

findings.finding: CFO transition: Patrick Thompson stepped down as CFO effective 2026-10-01 and leaves employment 2026-10-30. Tigran Sinanyan, CFO 2015-2021 and SVP Finance since July 2025, takes over, so this is the first call under the new CFO. The filing says the change is not due to any disagreement.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since September, and announced alongside the guide raise, so largely priced. The residual risk is a more conservative first Q4 guide from a new CFO.

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is up 22.57% over 20 days (to $11.73 from about $9.40 on 2026-09-25), including +9.3% on 2026-10-15 with no cited cause. Short interest rose 13.7% to 6.16% of float (2.8 days to cover) by 2026-10-15. Last quarter the stock fell 1.88% on a beat-and-raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-29: beat and raise, -1.88%. Other reactions are ±10-18% with no clean pattern against run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The question is whether the run-up already discounts the pre-announced beat. The skew (-10, upside paid) points the other way, but the chain's 96% spread makes it unreadable. Short interest is not crowded, so a squeeze is not a strong counter-mechanism.
findings.independence: Short-interest series: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MAX/short-interest/ (2026-10-26). The run-up is also in the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Insiders sold steadily under 10b5-1 plans into the print. Per MarketBeat, 419,925 shares worth about $5.2m in the 90 days to mid-October. EDGAR shows Form 144s filed 2026-10-08, 10-13, 10-16, 10-19 (x2) and 10-26, and CEO Nonko's 13D/A of 2026-08-26 shows a net 725k-share decrease to 9.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None sourced; this selling has been continuous across up and down prints.
findings.why_not_priced: These are routine pre-arranged plans, carry almost no information, and are visible to anyone.

findings.finding: Allstate, a likely top-3 MAX customer, reported Q3 2026 catastrophe losses of $1.65bn pre-tax ($220m in September) in its 2026-10-15 monthly release. The release has no growth or advertising commentary. Cat load bears on carriers' appetite to buy customer acquisition, but I could not source a prior-year comparison.
findings.why_not_priced: Without a year-ago comparison I cannot sign it. Filed at 0 so a judge with that comparison can size it.

outside_window.finding: Progressive's Q3 2026 10-Q, which quantifies quarterly advertising spend (Q1 +20%, Q2 +16% to $1.4bn), is not yet filed and normally lands in early November.

baseline_tension: The 22.6% run-up and the unusable but upside-leaning skew both say the market has already taken in the pre-announced beat. My filed findings lean slightly negative on Q4-guide risk, which cuts mildly against the run-up's optimism, but the evidence is proxy-level, so p_up stays at 51.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6/1: the pre-announcement lands inside what the company already guided and the bar sources disagree ($347.7m vs $353.8m), so it was cut from +0.8 to +0.4.
Lesson 2: the TRA buyout gain is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it was cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
Lessons 5/9: the Progressive proxy is a direct counterparty in a primary document but unconfirmed by MAX; sized net of the 3rd-5th carrier diversification, -1.0 to -0.8.

Lesson 7: short interest was looked up (6.16%, not crowded), so the run-up positioning negative was trimmed only from -0.8 to -0.6. The CFO, insider and Q4-decel items were trimmed slightly as already public.

EverQuote buyback trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4 because it is a proxy. abs_move_pct lowered from 12 to 11 because the quarter is pre-released (core table), and p_up raised from 50 to 51 because the company-level document is positive.
